---
title: "Randomized study on puzzle solving"
params:
  lang: "en"
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

hook(s2_pool, subscript(s^2L, pool))
hook(mu_A, subscript(mean(X), "A"))
hook(mu_B, subscript(mean(X), "B"))
hook(n_A, subscript(n, "A"))
hook(n_B, subscript(n, "B"))
hook(s_A, subscript(s, "A"))
hook(s_B, subscript(s, "B"))

task <- "tgroups6"
plfile <- file.path("rexams", sprintf("%s.pl", task))
rolog::consult(system.file(plfile, package="mistakes"))


## DATA GENERATION
repeat
{
  n_A <- sample(20:40, 1)
  n_B <- n_A + sample(5:15, 1)

  mu_A <- round(runif(1, 12, 20), 1)
  mu_B <- round(runif(1, 8, 15), 1)

  s_A <- round(runif(1, 5, 8), 1)
  s_B <- round(runif(1, 2, 4), 1)

  tratio <- (mu_A - mu_B) / sqrt(s_A^2/n_A + s_B^2/n_B)

  if(abs(tratio) < 0.5 || abs(tratio) > 3.0)
    next

  Q <- quote(search(tgroups6, welch(mu_A, s_A, n_A, mu_B, s_B, n_A), .S, .R, .P, .E))
  S <- findall(Q, options = list(preproc = as.rolog), env = environment())

  if(problems(S))
    next

  break
}



tab <- data.frame(
  "Condition A" = c(sprintf("%.0f", n_A), sprintf("%.1f", mu_A), sprintf("%.1f", s_A)), 
  "Condition B" = c(sprintf("%.0f", n_B), sprintf("%.1f", mu_B), sprintf("%.1f", s_B)),
  check.names = FALSE
)

row.names(tab) <- c("Sample size", "Mean completion time (min)", "Standard deviation (min)")


t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(
  t$correct, t$explanations, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra
)
```


Question
========
In a social psychology experiment on frustration and task performance, 
participants were randomly assigned to two conditions. 
In Condition A, participants completed a series of unsolvable puzzles 
designed to induce frustration, in Condition B, participants completed solvable puzzles. 
After a short break, all participants were given a set of new puzzles. 
The time needed to complete these (in minutes) was the primary outcome of the study. 
Consider the following data: 

````{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(tab, align=c("c", "c", "l"))
````
Because greater variability in task performance is expected in Condition A, 
calculate the Welch statistic for the difference between the group averages.
A positive Welch-statistic should indicate superiority of the no-frustration group.

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The Welch-statistic is calculated by: `r t$solution`

```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
